text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Some Malawians working for Asian shop owners in Blantyre are accusing their masters of ill-treating and underpaying them at K50 per week ($3) and ordering them to leave if they grumble openly.

- The opposition Malawi Congress Party's (MCP) treasurer general said at a rally in Lilongwe over the week-end that former president Kamuzu Banda has instructed that 230 hectares of his cattle ranch in Lower Shire Valley be distributed to the local people.
- Retired army officers and men including two former generals have formed an association to relay concerns of ex-servicemen to government.

- Main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) is to protest to the Electoral Commission this week against unfair campaign strategies employed by the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) for the May 26 by-elections in six constituencies.

- Embittered Malawi Congress of Trade Union officials, unleashing unkind words, said on Sunday they would be too happy if Justice Minister Cassim Chilumpha, who is chairman of the cabinet committee on the economy, stopped meddling in genuine efforts to revive wage talks which failed last Friday.
- Two curio vendors were over the week-end drugged by a couple claiming to be South Africans and robbed off K20,000 ($1,333) in a foreign currency black marketeering deal.
- Dissatisfied junior police officers are said to be circulating a letter calling for a nationwide strike aimed at forcing government to address a string of their grievances.

- President of the opposition Alliance for Democracy (AFORD) Chakufwa Chihana told a rally over the week-end that plans for his party to merge with main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) have reached an advanced stage.
